newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SACCHI FAILS TO WORK MIRACLES AT MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SACCHI FAILS TO WORK MIRACLES AT MILAN.

text.p: Almost two months after resigning as Italian national team coach to return to ailing AC Milan, Arrigo Sacchi has so far failed to work miracles.
On Sunday, Milan touched a new low when they lost 3-1 to second from bottom Verona to sink to 10th place in serie A, seven points above the relegation zone.

Since Sacchi returned to coach the club in the first week of December, Milan have lost four out of eight competitive matches and they have now lost as many league matches this season as they have won.
Losses to Parma, Lazio and Verona in serie A were painful enough but a Champions League' elimination by Norwegian side Rosenborg in Sacchi's first game in charge was even more costly.
Inevitably, Italian sports critics were scathing in their Monday analysis of the loss at Verona:
"It's now official, Milan does not exist", headlined Milan based sports daily Gazzetta dello Sport, while Rome based sports daily Corriere dello Sport crowed: "Milan, you've only got your memories".
Rome daily La Repubblica says Sacchi is not the ideal man to step into an emergency situation which requires short term solutions.
"We think that Milan got the timing (not to mention the manner) of Sacchi's return very wrong. He's the sort of coach who wants to build together a team and for that you need time to work.
"He's not a coach suited to stop-gap remedies. In this case, the patient is no better after the initial treatment".
Two months after returning to the Milan side which he led to Italian and European success in the late 1980s, Sacchi still seems unsure of his ideal selection.

Talented players such as Roberto Baggio and Montenegrin Dejan Savicevic have been in and out of the side while new recruits like Dutch defender Michael Reiziger, Swedish midfielder Jesper Blomqvist, Dutch midfielder Edgar Davids and French striker Christophe Dugarry have all failed to play to their best.
Nor has Sacchi been helped by an injury to the club's outstanding talent, Liberian striker George Weah, who has been sidelined for the last three weeks.

Speaking after Sunday's defeat, Sacchi commented said: "For six months, things have been going badly here. We're back to where we were with my predecessor, (Oscar) Tabarez... I assume all my own personal responsibility for not being able to improve things".
Club captain and standard bearer Franco Baresi was equally despondent.
"Other teams run more than us while we managed to concede three goals in counter attacks," he said. "We just leave the door open and it is all too easy for our opponents to score."
On Monday, Milan travel to Holland to play in a four-club, six-a-side tournament hosted by Dutch side Ajax Amsterdam and featuring Scottish side Glasgow Rangers and English league leaders Liverpool.
Milan will hope for a welcome respite in Amsterdam because when they return to serie A next Sunday, it will be to face second placed Sampdoria, arguably the most in-form side in the league.
Winners of five out of their last six games, Sampdoria are four points behind leaders Juventus and seven points clear of Milan.
